summary: Malcolm David Eckel is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Oxford and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and held faculty posts at Harvard (1980–1991) and Boston University (1990–2024).
Mamata Dash is an Indology scholar. She was educated at Ravenshaw Girls' High School and Utkal University.

Mamoru Tonami was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Ichisada Miyazaki, later serving there as assistant (1965), associate professor (1975), and professor (1984, 1993, 1996–2001).
Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist. He served as Secretary of The Asiatic Society and was the DSA Sanskrit Co-ordinator at Jadavpur University (attested 2003).

Manfred B. Steger works in religious studies, philosophy, and political science. After studying at the University of Hawaiʻi and Rutgers University, he taught at Illinois State (1996–2005), RMIT University (2005–2011), and the University of Hawaiʻi (2011–2016).

Manfred Mayrhofer was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Graz under Wilhelm Brandenstein, later holding professorships at Saarland University (1962–1966) and the University of Vienna (1966–1990).

Manfred Taube was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Friedrich Weller at Leipzig University (1949–1953), where he was appointed Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology in 1991.

Manshi Kiyozawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Francisco Fenollosa, he served as principal of Kyoto Prefectural Middle School (1888) and became the founding president of Otani University (~1901–1902).
Manu Leumann was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Munich (~1922–1927) and the University of Zurich (~1927–1959).

Marc Aurel Stein was a scholar of archaeology, history, and Iranian, Central Asian, and Indology studies. He completed his PhD under Rudolf von Roth at Tübingen and held posts at the University of the Punjab and Archaeological Survey of India.
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist. He studied under Nahid Rouzbeh and completed his PhD at the University of Lausanne under the supervision of Johannes Bronkhorst.

Marc-Henri Deroche specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He pursued doctoral studies supervised by Matthew T. Kapstein, and studied under Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcel Cohen was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He held long-term posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris (~1919–1955), as well as L'Humanité (~1944–1974).

Marcel Granet was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes, and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1922–1940) and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises (~1927–1940).

Marcel Mauss was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied under Émile Durkheim, Sylvain Lévi, and others, and held chairs at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 1901) and the Collège de France (1931–1940).

Marcelle Lalou was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed her doctorate at the EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, Jacques Bacot, Paul Pelliot, and Jean Przyluski. She taught at the EPHE (1938–1963) and edited the Journal Asiatique (1950–1966).
Marco Walther is a scholar of Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Munich (attested 2017) under the supervision of Franz-Karl Ehrhard, and also studied under Khenpo Dondrup Namgyal.

Marcus Bingenheimer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his doctoral studies under Norbert Klaes at the University of Würzburg, later holding positions at the Dharma Drum Institute (2005–2011) and Temple University (2012–2015).

Marek Mejor was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held a fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford (1981–1982) and served as a professor at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2010).

Marek Zemánek works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dongguk University, Seoul National University, and completed his dissertation at Charles University under the supervision of Radek Chlup.
